survey: Image 4 is a lumpy brown asteroid floating in mid-air against a wavy blue background, with no ground. The camera sits slightly above and to the front-left of the rock. Its front-left face is turned toward the viewer, and the top and right side curve away. Three orange teardrop flames come out from behind the upper-right of the rock. They trail up and to the right, so the rock reads as flying toward the lower-left. Each flame tapers to a point with a small droplet in line with its tip, and the flames overlap from back to front in a believable order. Surface details: a large crater on the left front face, a medium crater in the centre, a dark crater cut by the lower silhouette, several pinpricks, a flattened facet on the right, and a hairline crack on top. The large crater's rim is a tall ellipse and you can see its inner wall on the right side, which matches a surface turning away to the left. The centre crater is a near-round ellipse because it faces the camera. The bottom crater is wider than it is tall, which fits a surface turning downward. The pinpricks get slightly flatter toward the edges. The flames all leave from the same rear area and point the same way, so they agree with one direction of travel and one camera. With no ground, there is no contact to check.
